subject: Chemistry
title: Novichok: The Russian Nerve Agent
description: A short lesson to help you apply Novichok: The Russian Nerve Agent.

hook.text: In 2018, a former Russian spy and his daughter collapsed on a park bench in Salisbury, England.

buildup.text: They were poisoned with Novichok—a nerve agent 5 to 10 times more potent than sarin.

discovery.text: Like sarin, Novichok blocks acetylcholinesterase. But it binds more tightly and is harder to reverse.

twist.text: The poison was smeared on a door handle. A police officer who investigated also became seriously ill.

climax.text: Months later, a woman died after her partner found a discarded perfume bottle containing Novichok in a bin.

punchline.text: A nerve agent that lingers on surfaces for months. Deadlier than sarin.

quiz.question: How was Novichok delivered in the 2018 Salisbury poisoning?
options: Smeared on the front door handle of the victims' home
Injected with a poisoned umbrella tip

details.summary: Novichok agents are a class of fourth-generation nerve agents developed by the Soviet Union that are estimated to be five to ten times more potent than VX nerve agent. They inhibit acetylcholinesterase irreversibly and were designed to evade NATO chemical detection equipment.
details.whyItMatters: The 2018 Novichok poisoning of Sergei Skripal in England demonstrated that advanced nerve agents remain active threats. The incident prompted global reevaluation of chemical weapons detection protocols.
takeaways: Novichok agents are five to ten times more potent than VX
They were designed to bypass Western chemical detection systems
The Skripal poisoning triggered major diplomatic consequences

faq.question: How do Novichok agents differ from older nerve agents like sarin?
faq.answer: Novichok agents bind more tightly to acetylcholinesterase and are more resistant to standard antidotes like pralidoxime. Some variants can penetrate protective equipment more effectively. They were also designed as binary weapons, with two less-toxic precursors combining to form the agent.

faq.question: How did Sergei Skripal survive a Novichok poisoning?
faq.answer: Rapid medical intervention at Salisbury District Hospital, including mechanical ventilation and aggressive atropine and pralidoxime treatment, kept Skripal alive through the critical period. The exposure dose may have been lower than intended..
